title: sopuli-dba configuration
description:
A sopuli-dba configuration file (docs/design/01-configuration.md).

Structural only, and deliberately so. It describes key names, types, closed sets, required keys, and rejects unknown keys -- which is what makes editor completion and P3's "a typo in a credential tool must never be silently ignored" work while somebody is typing.

The rules it does not express are enforced by `sopuli config validate`, whose errors name the offending key: the inline form and `applications:` are mutually exclusive; `secret` and `secret_template` are mutually exclusive; two accounts may not resolve to one secret ref; `require:` may not exceed `length:` or ask for specials a charset does not have; `allow:` belongs to `charset: custom`; an `auth:` block may carry only the keys its own `method:` takes; every vault, policy, group, profile and target name written anywhere must be declared in the section that declares it; a `for_each` must use one inner dimension throughout; and a profile may not set a key that would change scope. A file this schema accepts may still be refused there.

version.description: The config schema version this file is written for. Required: a file with no version cannot be migrated later (§9a).

applications.description: The binding, for one or more applications (§3).

secret.description: A SecretRef (01-configuration.md §7): [vault:]path[#field][/pointer][@qualifier]. In `secret_template` the {tokens} are expanded per account and target.

secret_template.description: A SecretRef (01-configuration.md §7): [vault:]path[#field][/pointer][@qualifier]. In `secret_template` the {tokens} are expanded per account and target.

policy.description: The name of an entry in `policies:`.

safety.description: Safety settings only ratchet toward safe: the resolved value is the lowest max_targets, the union of confirm_environments, and readonly if any layer sets it (00-principles.md P3, invariant 10).

vault.description: One named secret store. Only `type` is required: the backends differ enough that demanding a HashiCorp shape of every entry would be the vendor bias P1 forbids, so per-backend requirements live behind the store interface.

oneOf.description: Shorthand for `{ method: NAME }`, available where the method needs nothing else.

non_production.description: Absent means production. A target with environment: prod pointed at a store marked here is refused (§10).

vault_auth.description: How to authenticate, and where the material comes from -- never the material itself (P2). Each method takes only its own keys, which the validator checks; the identity fields are inline and everything secret-bearing is a MaterialRef.

mount.description: The auth mount, not the KV mount on the vault itself. Defaults to the method's own name.

material_ref.description: Where a piece of auth material comes from: an environment variable or a file. Not a SecretRef -- this is what you need before you have a vault.

vault.description: The name of an entry in `vaults:`.

admin.description: Which credential reaches the database, never the password: storing the admin password in the config file is not supported at all (P2).

username.description: Absent under `auth: external`, where the wallet supplies it, and overridable per execution context by SOPULI_DB_ADMIN_USER (§6).

oneOf.description: Shorthand for `{ method: NAME }`, available where the method needs nothing else.

admin_auth.description: P2's bootstrap sources, in its order of preference: external authentication, a vault path, an interactive prompt, an environment variable.

password_env.description: The variable holding the admin password, for `method: env`. Defaults to SOPULI_DB_ADMIN_PASSWORD. Still low-assurance (P2).

secret.description: For `method: vault`: a full SecretRef, so it takes a `vault:` prefix and §7's tokens. Defaults to the target's own vault.

target_oracle.description: Which container the tool connects to. Not an application's `oracle:` block, which carries `container_clause` -- same key name, different meaning.

target_set.description: A target template plus the dimensions to expand it over (§4). Listing 35 PDBs by hand is not viable; this generates them.

name.description: The name *template*, e.g. appdb-{env}-{tenant}. The key this entry is written under is the set's own name.

vault.description: The name of an entry in `vaults:`.

overrides.description: Patches keyed by rendered target name (§4 rule 5).

target_patch.description: What to change about one generated target. `name` is absent because the rendered name is the key this patch is found by, so patching it would make the key a lie.

vault.description: The name of an entry in `vaults:`.

for_each.description: Exactly one outer dimension, named by its key; under it, one entry per value of that dimension, holding the variables in scope for it (§4 rule 1).

additionalProperties.description: A scalar substituted into the templates, or a list -- which makes it the inner dimension, at most one per value (§4 rules 2 and 6).

group.description: A name for a label selection over the estate (§4).

policy.description: Password rules, rotation strategy and verification, under one name.

password_policy.description: §8's charsets and the character classes a password must contain.

allow.description: Belongs to `charset: custom` and to nothing else. May not contain " -- Oracle quoted identifiers have no escape for it (invariant 11).

require.description: Minimum count per character class. A block no password of this length and charset could satisfy is refused by the validator, not here.

rotation_policy.description: How a new password replaces the old one (UC-1 §6).

verify_policy.description: How the tool confirms a password works. Shared with a profile, because the same estate is verified by login from a laptop and by hash comparison from a scheduler (§5).

account_policy.description: What the tool may do to the account itself.

profile.description: Where a run is invoked from -- `interactive`, `ci`, `scheduled` -- never what it points at. Everything here changes how the tool behaves; nothing here changes which targets or accounts are in scope (§5).

vault.description: The name of an entry in `vaults:`.

profile_rotation.description: Only `strategy`. The rest of a rotation policy describes the credential's lifecycle, which is a property of the estate rather than of the machine running the command.

profile_db.description: Budgets that differ when nobody is waiting.

defaults.description: Precedence layer 5 (P3): the bottom of the config file.

vault.description: The name of an entry in `vaults:`.

runtime.description: How this installation of the tool is set up, not what it manages.

runtime_oracle.description: Where the Instant Client lives. Thick mode is a runtime prerequisite on every platform (P4, D3).

application.description: These accounts, in these targets, mastered by these secrets, under this policy -- the sentence §1 says the whole config exists to state.

vault.description: The name of an entry in `vaults:`.

secret.description: A SecretRef (01-configuration.md §7): [vault:]path[#field][/pointer][@qualifier]. In `secret_template` the {tokens} are expanded per account and target.

secret_template.description: A SecretRef (01-configuration.md §7): [vault:]path[#field][/pointer][@qualifier]. In `secret_template` the {tokens} are expanded per account and target.

policy.description: The name of an entry in `policies:`.

accounts.description: The database accounts this application owns. Invariant 5: the config is the whitelist, so nothing outside this list is ever touched.

oneOf.description: Target names, against the expanded estate.

group.description: The name of an entry in `groups:`.

application_targets.description: Which targets this entry applies to. Absent means all of them.

oracle_options.description: How `ALTER USER` is written for these accounts. Not a target's `oracle:` block, which says which container to connect to.

overrides.description: Per-label exceptions to this entry's own resolution (§2, §3).

override.description: `accounts` is not patchable, and that is a rule rather than an omission: invariant 5 says selectors filter the declared set and cannot extend it, not even under --force.

where.description: Which targets the patch applies to.

vault.description: The name of an entry in `vaults:`.

secret.description: A SecretRef (01-configuration.md §7): [vault:]path[#field][/pointer][@qualifier]. In `secret_template` the {tokens} are expanded per account and target.

secret_template.description: A SecretRef (01-configuration.md §7): [vault:]path[#field][/pointer][@qualifier]. In `secret_template` the {tokens} are expanded per account and target.

policy.description: The name of an entry in `policies:`.
